paper.task: A graph attentional layer takes a set of node features h (N nodes, F features each) together with each node's graph neighborhood and produces a new set of node features h' (F' features per node, KF' with concatenated heads); stacked into graph attention networks (GAT) for transductive and inductive node classification.

components.name: node features h
components.what: the layer's input: a set of N node feature vectors h_1..h_N, each h_i in R^F

provenance.quote: The input to our layer is a set of node features

components.name: neighborhood N_i
components.what: the graph structure: for each node i its neighborhood N_i, in all experiments the first-order neighbors of i including i itself

provenance.quote: where N i is some neighborhood of node i in the graph. In all our experiments, these will be exactly the first-order neighbors of i (including i)

components.name: graph attentional layer
components.what: the sole building-block layer of every GAT architecture (networks are built by stacking it); maps h to h' with K attention heads

provenance.quote: We will start by describing a single graph attentional layer, as the sole layer utilized throughout all of the GAT architectures used in our experiments

components.name: attention head
components.what: one of K independent attention mechanisms, each executing the transformation of Eq. (4) with its own W^k and a^k; recorded once, repeated K times (e.g. K = 8 in the transductive first layer, K = 4 in the inductive hidden layers)

provenance.quote: Specifically, K independent attention mechanisms execute the transformation of Equation 4

components.name: shared linear transformation W
components.what: weight matrix W in R^{F'xF} applied to every node, h_i -> W h_i (W^k in head k)

provenance.quote: linear transformation, parametrized by a weight matrix, W ∈ R F ×F , is applied to every node

components.name: attentional mechanism a
components.what: shared mechanism a: R^F' x R^F' -> R computing attention coefficients e_ij = a(W h_i, W h_j); a single-layer feedforward network; setup follows Bahdanau et al. (2015); a^k in head k

provenance.quote: a shared attentional mechanism a : R F × R F → R computes attention coefficients

components.name: concatenation
components.what: concatenates the transformed pair: [W h_i || W h_j]

provenance.quote: where · T represents transposition and k is the concatenation operation

components.name: weight vector a
components.what: the single-layer feedforward network's weights: inner product a^T [W h_i || W h_j], with a in R^{2F'}

provenance.quote: parametrized by a weight vector ~ a ∈ R 2F

components.name: LeakyReLU
components.what: nonlinearity with negative input slope 0.2 applied to a^T[W h_i || W h_j]; its output is the attention coefficient e_ij

provenance.quote: applying the LeakyReLU nonlinearity (with negative input slope α = 0.2)

components.name: masked attention
components.what: injects the graph structure: e_ij is computed only for nodes j in N_i (instead of every node attending to every other node)

provenance.quote: We inject the graph structure into the mechanism by performing masked attention

components.name: softmax
components.what: normalizes e_ij across all j in N_i into the normalized attention coefficients alpha_ij (Eq. 2)

provenance.quote: we normalize them across all choices of j using the softmax function

components.name: linear combination
components.what: attention-weighted sum over the neighborhood: sum_{j in N_i} alpha_ij W h_j (Eq. 4)

provenance.quote: the normalized attention coefficients are used to compute a linear combination of the features corresponding to them

components.name: nonlinearity σ
components.what: optional ('potentially') nonlinearity applied to each head's linear combination, giving that head's output features h'_i (Eq. 4, inside the concatenation of Eq. 5); ELU after the hidden layers in the experiments (Sec. 3.3)

provenance.quote: after potentially applying a nonlinearity, σ

components.name: concatenation
components.what: concatenates the K heads' output features (Eq. 5), so h' has KF' features per node

provenance.quote: and then their features are concatenated, resulting in the following output feature representation

components.name: averaging
components.what: used instead of concatenation on the final (prediction) layer: averages the K heads' linear combinations, (1/K) sum_k (Eq. 6)

provenance.quote: concatenation is no longer sensible—instead, we employ averaging

components.name: final nonlinearity σ
components.what: on the final (prediction) layer, applied only after averaging the heads; usually a softmax or logistic sigmoid for classification

provenance.quote: delay applying the final nonlinearity (usually a softmax or logistic sigmoid for classification problems) until then

train_vs_infer.what: in the transductive setup, dropout (p = 0.6) is applied during training to both layers' inputs and to the normalized attention coefficients alpha_ij, so each node sees a stochastically sampled neighborhood per training iteration

provenance.quote: dropout (Srivastava et al., 2014) with p = 0.6 is applied to both layers’ inputs, as well as to the normalized attention coefficients (critically, this means that at each training iteration, each node is exposed to a stochastically sampled neighborhood)

train_vs_infer.what: in the inductive setup the model is evaluated on test graphs that remain completely unobserved during training

provenance.quote: Critically, testing graphs remain completely unobserved during training

contributions.text: the graph attentional layer: a building-block layer from which arbitrary graph attention networks are constructed by stacking

provenance.quote: we will present the building block layer used to construct arbitrary graph attention networks (through stacking this layer)

contributions.text: computationally efficient: the self-attentional layer parallelizes across all edges and output features across all nodes; no eigendecompositions

provenance.quote: Computationally, it is highly efficient: the operation of the self-attentional layer can be parallelized across all edges, and the computation of output features can be parallelized across all nodes

contributions.text: unlike GCNs, assigns (implicitly) different importances to nodes of the same neighborhood

provenance.quote: As opposed to GCNs, our model allows for (implicitly) assigning different importances to nodes of a same neighborhood

contributions.text: attention is shared across all edges, so it needs no upfront access to the global graph structure: works for directed graphs and inductive learning on unseen graphs

provenance.quote: The attention mechanism is applied in a shared manner to all edges in the graph, and therefore it does not depend on upfront access to the global graph structure

contributions.text: works with the entirety of the neighborhood and assumes no ordering within it

provenance.quote: Our technique does not suffer from either of these issues—it works with the entirety of the neighborhood

contributions.text: uses node features, not structural properties, for similarity computations

provenance.quote: our model uses node features for similarity computations, rather than the node’s structural properties

unclear: Extraction lost primes and the concatenation symbol: 'F 0' / 'h 0' read as F' / h'; 'k' inside [W ~h i kW ~h j ] and the leading 'k' in Eq. (5) are the concatenation symbol ||, while other 'k' are the head index. Eq. (3)'s numerator and denominator are interleaved; read as exp(LeakyReLU(a^T[W h_i || W h_j])) / sum_{k in N_i} exp(LeakyReLU(a^T[W h_i || W h_k])).

Where masked attention acts is stated only as 'we only compute e ij for nodes j ∈ N i'; the text does not say whether it restricts which pairs enter a or masks e_ij before the softmax. The softmax (Eq. 2) and the linear combination (Eq. 4) also range over N_i. Recorded as graph_nbhd -> mask -> att_a (control).
The text calls only the node features 'the input to our layer'; the graph structure (N_i) enters via masked attention, so graph_nbhd is recorded with role 'data', not 'io'.

Two output paths: hidden layers apply σ per head and concatenate the K heads (Eq. 5); the final (prediction) layer averages the heads' linear combinations and applies σ (softmax / logistic sigmoid) after averaging (Eq. 6). With a single head (e.g. the transductive output layer) Eq. (4)'s σ output is the layer output directly.

Novelty: the attention setup 'closely follows' Bahdanau et al. (2015) and multi-head attention follows Vaswani et al. (2017), so att_a and its parts are 'reused'; the head is marked 'proposed' as the core computation of the proposed layer (Eqs. 1-4), which is a judgement, not an explicit claim.

Section 1 (introduction) is not in the text, so no explicit contribution list was available; contributions are taken from the claims in Sec. 2 and 2.2. The text also jumps mid-sentence into Sec. 3 ('well as inductive), achieving or matching...'): the start of the evaluation section is missing.
Sec. 2.1 refers to 'Figure 1 (left)' (attention mechanism) and 'Figure 1 (right)' (multi-head aggregation); blind run, their content is unknown and not used.

Experiment-specific additions, not part of the layer definition and not recorded as components or flows: dropout on layer inputs and on alpha_ij (transductive training), skip connections across the intermediate attentional layer (inductive model), ELU as σ after hidden layers, and Const-GAT's constant attention a(x, y) = 1.
Training loss (cross-entropy on the training nodes) acts on the network's final output, outside the focus layer; left out of losses.
